hero.title: Doing business with faith for Africa's development
hero.subtitle: The Catholic Business Network of Africa (CBNA) brings together entrepreneurs, project leaders and partners who put entrepreneurship at the service of the common good.
hero.label: 5th promise of the Sacred Heart of Jesus
hero.photo: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace, Yamoussoukro

welcome.title: A community of entrepreneurs on a mission
welcome.p1: Our community brings together entrepreneurs, project leaders and partners committed to putting entrepreneurship at the service of Africa's development.
welcome.p2: We draw on devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus and the Immaculate Heart of Mary, on the intercession of the saints and angels, and on Christian values: integrity, solidarity, justice and the common good.

promise.title: The Sacred Heart's promise to entrepreneurs
promise.quote: I will pour abundant blessings upon all their undertakings.
promise.source: Promises of Our Lord Jesus Christ to Saint Margaret Mary Alacoque, Paray-le-Monial
promise.text: Among the promises made to those devoted to his Sacred Heart, the fifth speaks directly to those who undertake. It lies at the heart of our network: we entrust our projects, our businesses and our teams to the Sacred Heart of Jesus.
promise.listTitle: The promises of the Sacred Heart
items: I will give them all the graces necessary in their state of life.
I will establish peace in their families.
I will comfort them in all their afflictions.
I will be their secure refuge during life, and above all in death.
I will pour abundant blessings upon all their undertakings.
Sinners will find in my Heart the source and infinite ocean of mercy.
Fervent souls shall rise to great perfection.
I will bless every home in which the image of my Heart is exposed and honoured.
I will give to priests the gift of touching the most hardened hearts.

hero.title: About us
hero.subtitle: Catholic Business Network of Africa (CBNA), also known as Réseau des Entrepreneurs Catholiques d'Afrique (RECA).

who.title: A network of Catholic entrepreneurs serving Africa
who.p1: CBNA / RECA is a non-profit, non-political association headquartered in Yaoundé, Cameroon.
who.p2: It brings together entrepreneurs, project leaders and partners who want to make business a place of human, economic and spiritual growth, in the light of the social teaching of the Church.
who.p3: The network is organised into national sections and diaspora chapters, and works in both French and English.

heart.title: The Sacred Heart of Jesus
heart.text: We entrust our businesses to the Sacred Heart, faithful to the promise made to Saint Margaret Mary Alacoque: "I will pour abundant blessings upon all their undertakings."

mary.title: The Immaculate Heart of Mary
mary.text: We turn to Mary, an attentive mother, to guide our work, our families and our communities.

items.title: Integrity
items.text: Acting with honesty and transparency in all our business relationships.

items.title: Solidarity
items.text: Supporting one another and leaving no one behind.

items.title: Justice
items.text: Seeking fairness in work, trade and the sharing of its fruits.

items.title: Common good
items.text: Making business a driver of development for the whole of society.

items.title: General Assembly
items.text: The sovereign body that brings members together and sets the main directions.

items.title: Executive Board
items.text: Implements decisions and leads the life of the network.

items.title: Ethics and Discernment Council
items.text: Ensures the Code of Ethics and the association's values are respected.

items.title: National sections and diaspora chapters
items.text: Bring the network to life close to its members, in each country.

hero.title: Membership
hero.subtitle: Join the Catholic Business Network of Africa.

membership.intro: Membership is open to Catholic entrepreneurs living in Africa or in the diaspora, and to people of goodwill who share our values.

items.name: Active members
items.text: Catholic entrepreneurs with paid-up dues. They can vote and stand for election.

items.name: Junior members
items.text: Young entrepreneurs in the mentoring programme. They become active members when they reach the age limit.

items.name: Associate members
items.text: People of goodwill, non-Catholics or non-entrepreneurs, who commit to respecting the ethics charter.

items.name: Benefactor members
items.text: Individuals or organisations who support the network materially or financially.

items.name: Honorary members
items.text: Appointed by the General Assembly for outstanding service.

items.title: Get in touch
items.text: Write to us or contact your country's section to receive the membership form.

items.title: Be sponsored
items.text: Your application is sponsored by two active members who know you.

items.title: Prepare your file
items.text: Attach the required documents and the signed Code of Ethics.

items.title: Board decision
items.text: The Executive Board reviews your application and notifies you of its decision.

docs.title: Required documents
items: Proof of business activity (registration, tax number or equivalent)
Baptism certificate or a sworn statement
For the diaspora: evidence of your bond with your country of origin
For an organisation: the appointment of its representative

membership.note: Membership and annual fees are set by the General Assembly. Contact us for the current rates.
